groups.title: Products and apps
projects: Two-minute skill checks in 40-plus fields, scored Elo-style, with peer percentiles and three LLM features. Full stack on $0 a month.
EV trip planner for a five-year-old battery: range adjusted for elevation and weather, and a detour budget for avoiding risky turns.
What it takes to be top 1%, top 10% or median: 950 facts from 72 sources, each graded A to D, with the distribution drawn underneath.
Any picture or prompt becomes one continuous line, drawn by a chain of rotating arrows in the browser.
Today's Hong Kong news rewritten into spoken Cantonese, with neural audio, jyutping and speech grading. Rebuilt daily.
A tutor built from any Chinese EPUB: pinyin over every character, read-aloud, and offline pronunciation grading.

groups.title: The fine-tuning series
projects: Wine label photo to a cited profile and pairings; a 1.5B LoRA names the grape from a blind tasting note.
Menu photo to translated dishes with cuisine and allergen tags, from a LoRA that needs no schema in the prompt.
Receipt photos to categorized spending; 90.5% category accuracy on merchants the model never saw.
Course map photo to a km-by-km pacing plan that has to pass six deterministic checks.

groups.title: Retrieval and agents
projects: Plain-English search over 30,000 wine reviews: BM25 plus dense retrieval and a reranker, about 21% better than dense alone.
A coach that calls my pace and heat models as tools, also served over MCP. On 42 frozen numeric checks it got 42 right, against 21 for plain RAG and 14 for the bare model.
A LangGraph agent that reasons from pairing principles to a style, searches the reviews and critiques its own pick.
A LangGraph agent that drafts a training plan and keeps revising it until it passes explicit safety checks.

groups.title: Running and athletics
projects: 80 Boston Marathons against ERA5 course weather: heat is free to 55°F, then costs about 0.4% of finish time per degree, with a live race-day forecast.
Only 2.5% of 31,912 Boston 2014 finishers ran a negative split; across eight Boston years the share runs from 2.4% to 10.8%.
Eight Boston years of 5 km splits and a live race predictor: enter splits as you pass each mat for a finish range and wall risk, tested on 2024.
Where any marathon time sits among 31,842 finishers, and how far out the world record is, using extreme-value theory.
Are Boston qualifying times equally hard for every age and gender group?
Three ways to rank the six Majors by difficulty, tested on simulated races with planted penalties.
How much of the recent drop in marathon times comes from the shoes.
Every Olympic event's world-record progression, a frailty survival model tested on 2011 to 2025, and the odds each current record falls before LA 2028.
Kruskal-Wallis tests on 6,400 elite marks: the best in some events score 68 points more than in others.
K-means and PCA on 43 nations across five disciplines, which fall into five profiles.

groups.title: Wine, words and money
projects: Nothing in about 120,000 unique reviews scores below 80, and 85% land between 84 and 92.
A season 1 °C warmer than normal moved scores by 0.24 points in cool regions, across 55,597 reviews and 55 regions. The checks weaken even that.
Hong Kong's five petrol brands post one price on 88% of days. Six years of posted prices screened against import costs, with Perth and Los Angeles for contrast.
Half the extra Wikipedia attention a death brings is gone about two days after the peak; a year later the page still draws 1.08 times its old traffic. 1,905 deaths and 178 awards, 2016 to 2025.
Fifty years of Billboard hits got longer and more repetitive, but the vocabulary held.
The top 100 words make up 61% of everything said; about 1,250 words cover 95%.
Grade level, vocabulary richness and a word-coverage curve for any EPUB, computed in the browser.
Replays your retirement plan through every start year of US market history since 1871, and finds the smallest change that reaches 90%.

groups.title: Small tools
projects: When to leave to arrive on time, from Google Maps traffic estimates.
A 45-minute layover at a US hub missed 17% of the time, from 23 million flights. The lookup gives the layover you need for 95%.
A desktop app for read-along audiobooks in English, Mandarin and Cantonese.
Turns a whole book or article into a two-host episode where every claim cites the sentences it came from and is checked before it is voiced.
A zero-dependency CLI that fills a long build with terminal trivia, then hands back the output untouched.

selected.label: Full-stack product
selected.headline: Skill checks scored like chess ratings
selected.text: SkillCompass gives two-minute quizzes in more than 40 fields and scores each answer Elo-style against the item's difficulty. You get a percentile against other test-takers, a map of what you know and a study plan. The backend is FastAPI on free tiers, so it costs nothing to keep running.
selected.figcap: SkillCompass, captured from the live site.

selected.label: Decision tool
selected.headline: Route planning for a five-year-old battery
selected.text: Leeway plans from the range your car has now, after five years of battery wear, and adjusts it for hills and weather. It keeps a hard reserve at every charger stop and spends a detour budget you set on avoiding unprotected left turns and rail crossings.
selected.figcap: Leeway's trip view, from its write-up.

selected.label: Survival analysis
selected.headline: Which world records fall before LA 2028?
selected.text: I rebuilt the ratified progression of all 46 Olympic events from World Athletics' records handbook, 1,251 reigns in all, and fitted a survival model with a frailty for each event. Fitted on what was known in 2010, it ranked the records that fell from 2011 to 2025 better than the base rate (Brier 0.235 against 0.329). Duplantis's pole vault leads the LA 2028 watchlist at 48%.
selected.figcap: The top of the LA 2028 watchlist, from the write-up.

selected.label: Regression
selected.headline: Heat starts costing Boston runners at 55°F
selected.text: Eighty Boston Marathons, 1940 to 2019, paired with ERA5 weather at three points on the course. Below 55°F the temperature costs nothing; above it the median runner loses about 0.42% of finish time per degree F. Dew point added nothing, and on the 2015 to 2019 holdout the model did no better than a flat guess, which the write-up says plainly.
selected.figcap: Each race against its long-run trend, by course temperature, 1940 to 2019.

selected.label: Language app
selected.headline: Learning spoken Cantonese from today's news
selected.text: Every day an LLM rewrites Hong Kong headlines from written Chinese into the Cantonese people speak, and a second pass reviews it. Each line comes with neural zh-HK audio and jyutping, plus tap-to-compare playback and speech grading.
selected.figcap: A lesson in the Cantonese Learner.

series.intro: Four photo-to-data apps. Each pairs an LLM pipeline with a small Qwen2.5 model I fine-tuned on my laptop (LoRA) for one step of the task, then benchmarks base, fine-tuned and Claude zero-shot on held-out data.

notes.a: Clean rerun on 2026-10-28: Claude saw only the merchant text and the 12 labels, with tools off. Most of its misses are noisy labels in the test set (hardware and cables marked other). The first run scored 56.0% with a leaked category list.
notes.b: Scored on the same 200 notes, the fine-tuned model is right on 55 and Claude on 46 (sign test p = 0.33), so the gap is within noise.
notes.c: Claude needs the full allergen schema in every prompt to get there; the fine-tuned model gets the dish name only.

stories.headline: The 100-point wine scale is an 8-point scale
stories.text: Across about 120,000 unique professional reviews (the source file repeats 9,983) nothing scores below 80, and 85% land between 84 and 92. Some critics are simply more generous than others.

stories.headline: Predicting the wall from the first few splits
stories.text: A model trained on 176,059 Boston finishers from 2014 to 2023 reads your splits as you pass each mat and gives a finish range and the chance of hitting the wall. On the unseen 2024 race it missed by 7.9 minutes at halfway, against 18.1 for even pace.
stories.figcap: The live split card on the write-up, mid-race.

stories.headline: Song lyrics got longer, not simpler
stories.text: Fifty years of Billboard hits doubled in length and grew more repetitive, while the vocabulary stayed about where it was.
